newsitem.title: UK: UK blocks bids for South West Water.
newsitem.headline: UK blocks bids for South West Water.

text.p: The UK department of trade and industry (DTI) said on Friday it had decided not to permit proposed bids for South West Water from Severn Trent and Wessex Water.

In a statement, DTI chief Ian Lang said he had decided to follow the recommendations of the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC), which had said such takeovers would be against the public interest.
Lang said the MMC "considered that prospective savings and other benefits to be expected from the merger were insufficient to offset this detriment to the public interest."
The move came as a surprise to the market, which had been expecting the DTI to allow the bids as long as price cuts of around 20 percent were promised by the bidders.
Shares in South West Water plunged on the news to be down 105.5 pence to 600 pence by 1009 GMT while Severn Trent gained 34.5 pence to 610 pence and Wessex was up 10.5 pence to 325 pence.

Wessex announced its intention to bid for its neighbouring water company on March 7 and Severn Trent tipped its hat into the ring on March 21, but both companies declined to put a price on their offers until the DTI had decided whether the bids could go ahead.
